This widens the gate to `geo` and `note`, and routes all three call sites through one helper so the right-click menu and the `?C` dialog cannot drift apart.

Stacked on #1427 (ENG-1356), which extracted `replaceShapeWithDiscourseNode`. **#1427 must merge first.** Base is that branch, so this diff is only what ENG-1884 adds.

## Reviewer brief

- **Result**: right-clicking a sticky note or a rectangle with text offers Convert To, prefilled with the shape's text. Empty ones do not. `text` and `image` behave as before.
- **Review focus**: `apps/roam/src/components/canvas/convertShapeToDiscourseNode.ts`. `getConvertibleShapeText` returns the dialog's initial text, or `null` when the shape cannot convert; every gate is now `!== null` on that one value, replacing the `isTextSelected || isImageSelected` booleans that lived in two files. The positioning block in `replaceShapeWithDiscourseNode` is the riskiest part, see below.
- **Risk**: no live-graph run. See Verification.

## Decisions worth challenging

- **Empty geo and note shapes are excluded.** FEE-824 asks for conversion "if it has text in it", and offering Convert To on every blank rectangle adds a submenu to the common case. Empty `text` shapes stay convertible, which is today's behavior, so this is not a regression for them. The asymmetry is deliberate.
- **Arrows are excluded** even though `TLArrowShapeProps` carries `text`. Arrows already convert to relations through the adjacent Relation submenu, and offering both on one shape invites picking the wrong one. ENG-1892 covers the Obsidian side; no ticket covers arrow labels.
- **`isImageSelected` survives in both files.** It no longer gates the submenu, but it still filters `page-node` out of the type list, which is about images lacking a key-image flag rather than about convertibility.
- **`"text" in shape.props` rather than a cast.** It narrows the props union, so `shape.props.text` types as `string` with no `as` and no optional chaining. Same idiom as `defaultHandleExternalTextContent.ts:79`. The preceding `TEXT_SHAPE_TYPES` check is the policy allow-list, not a redundant guard: it is what keeps arrows out.
- **Positioning changed in `replaceShapeWithDiscourseNode`, which is base-PR code.** It created the node with no `parentId`, and tldraw reads `x`/`y` as page coordinates when no parent is given (`Editor.createShapes`). A shape's `x`/`y` are parent-relative, so converting a shape inside a frame placed the node at the wrong point and re-parented it by hit test. Passing `parentId` alone is not enough: deleting one child of a two-shape group makes `GroupShapeUtil.onChildrenChange` dissolve the group, so the captured `parentId` stops resolving. The code now captures the page point before the delete and positions by it whenever the parent did not survive. Pre-existing for `text` and `image`, but `geo` and `note` are far likelier to sit in a frame or a group, which is why it is fixed here rather than deferred.

`replaceShapeWithDiscourseNode` deletes the source shape and creates a new one, so arrows bound to a converted shape unbind and dangle. Pre-existing for `text` and `image`, more reachable now. Not fixed here.

All three tasks done.

## Rebase

GitHub's `CONFLICTING` wasn't a textual conflict. The base branch had been **force-pushed**: rebased onto newer `main`, with two new commits and a `Revert` of one it previously had. My branch still carried the old copies, including the commit the base had since reverted. `git rebase --onto origin/<base> 71ef76484` replayed just my work and dropped the stale duplicates — **zero conflicts to resolve**. Branch is now exactly one logical change on top of the live base; PR went to `MERGEABLE`.

## Codex comments

Both were P2, both correct, both fixed and the threads replied to and resolved.

**Trimmed text** — I was passing `.trim()` to the dialog, so converting a deliberately indented text shape would silently rewrite its content. Trim now only decides whether a `geo`/`note` counts as empty; the dialog gets `props.text` unchanged.

**Missing `parentId`** — verified against the tldraw 2.4.6 source: `createShapes` treats `x`/`y` as *page* coordinates when no parent is given, but a shape inside a frame has frame-relative coords, so the node landed offset and got re-parented by hit test.

## Delegated full review

**No high or medium regressions.** It did catch that my `parentId` fix was incomplete, which I confirmed in `GroupShapeUtil.onChildrenChange`: deleting one child of a **two**-shape group dissolves the group, so the captured `parentId` stops resolving and tldraw falls back to exactly the misreading my comment claimed to prevent. The code now captures the page point before the delete and positions by it when the parent doesn't survive. I also fixed the dialog's rejection message, which didn't describe the shapes it actually accepts.

Two findings I deliberately **did not** act on, both design opinions rather than defects:
- `getConvertibleShapeText` returns `""` for images, an overloaded falsy sentinel. All three callers correctly use `!== null`; splitting it into a predicate plus a getter adds more surface than it removes. Worth your call.
- `ImageConvertOverlay`'s `isConvertibleImage` now duplicates the image branch of my helper. Deduping is awkward because the overlay needs a `shape is TLImageShape` type guard, which my helper can't provide.

I skipped its suggestion to type `TEXT_SHAPE_TYPES` — `TLShape["type"]` widens to `string`, so the annotation would catch no typos and would force a cast at the `.includes` call.

`pnpm ci:validate` green (6/6). PR body rewritten to cover the positioning change and why it touches base-PR code. **CI: 5 passing, 2 pending, 0 failing** — the app is tracking it, so I won't poll.

Two things still outstanding: `reviewDecision` is `CHANGES_REQUESTED` from the original Codex review, which should clear on re-review, and **the live Roam run still hasn't happened** — the Playwright harness needs those three `DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_*` keys in `apps/roam/.env`. The frame and group placement cases are now the ones most worth driving by hand.

content.text:
Neither is a bug — nothing misbehaves today. Both are "this could rot later" notes, which is why I left them. Here's what they actually touch.

There are **three** separate UI surfaces that all answer "can this shape become a discourse node":

| Surface | Where | Shapes |
|---|---|---|
| Right-click → **Convert To** submenu | `uiOverrides.tsx` `CustomContextMenu` | text, image, + now geo/note |
| **`?C`** keyboard dialog | `ConvertToDialog.tsx` | same set |
| Hover **icon button** on an image | `overlays/ImageConvertOverlay.tsx` (from base PR #1427) | images only |

My helper feeds the first two. The third has its own predicate.

## Finding A — the `""` return value

`getConvertibleShapeText` returns three different things:

```
null        → not convertible (locked, arrow, empty sticky, discourse node…)
""          → convertible, but has no text of its own  ← only images
"some text" → convertible, and this is the dialog's prefill
```

The catch: **`""` is falsy, but it means "yes, convertible"**. So the only correct test is `!== null`, which is what all three call sites do — [uiOverrides.tsx:411](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/uiOverrides.tsx:411), [uiOverrides.tsx:206](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/uiOverrides.tsx:206), [ConvertToDialog.tsx:28](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/ConvertToDialog.tsx:28).

The failure mode is a *future* edit. Someone writes the natural-looking `if (!shapeText) return` or `{convertibleText && (...)}`, and **images silently stop offering Convert To** in the right-click menu and the `?C` dialog. Empty text shapes too. No type error, no test failure — the menu item just quietly disappears for images.

There's a related smell at [uiOverrides.tsx:205](apps/roam/src/components/canvas/uiOverrides.tsx:205): for an image we compute `shapeText` (always `""`), then discard it and build `initialText` from the uploaded image URL instead. So on that path the return value is purely a gate.

The reviewer's suggestion was to split the two jobs — a boolean "is it convertible" and a separate "what's the prefill" — so there's no falsy-but-true value to trip over.

## Finding B — the duplicated image rule

"An image is convertible if it isn't locked" is now written in two places:

```ts
// ImageConvertOverlay.tsx:15 — governs the hover button
const isConvertibleImage = (shape?: TLShape | null): shape is TLImageShape =>
  shape?.type === "image" && !shape.isLocked;

// convertShapeToDiscourseNode.ts:17 — governs the menu + dialog
if (!shape || shape.isLocked) return null;
if (shape.type === "image") return "";
```

They agree today. The drift risk: if someone later decides, say, that an image whose asset failed to upload shouldn't be convertible, they fix whichever file they're in — and then **the hover button appears on an image the right-click menu refuses to convert**, or vice versa. Two surfaces of one feature disagreeing about the same image.

Why I didn't merge them: `isConvertibleImage` is a TypeScript **type guard** (`shape is TLImageShape`). The overlay depends on that narrowing — it stores the result as `TLImageShape` and hands it to `uploadImageShapeToRoam`, which won't accept a plain `TLShape`. My helper returns `string | null`, so it can't narrow anything. Sharing would mean the guard calls my helper *and* still repeats `type === "image"` for the narrowing, which is more code than the duplication costs.

Both are judgment calls rather than defects. If you want either tightened, A is the one I'd pick — the falsy-`""` trap is the kind of thing that bites silently, and splitting it is a contained change to one file plus three call sites.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph/.claude/skills/dg-roam-load-extension

# DG Roam Load Extension

Use this skill for one complete lifecycle: build `apps/roam`, open an authenticated slot, register `apps/roam/dist`, activate it, verify DG runtime readiness, run an optional caller test, capture proof, and close.

It composes with `dg-roam-playwright-session` for account/profile selection.

## Quick Start

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 1
```

Use another slot for isolated work:

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 2
```

The script builds by default, verifies `window.roamjs.extension.queryBuilder`, checks the DG settings UI, and writes proof under `local/roam-playwright/artifacts`.

To add feature-specific assertions without copying the loader, pass an ESM test module:

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 1 --test-module ./local/roam-playwright/feature-proof.mjs
```

```js
export default {
  readySelector: "[data-testid='feature-ready']",
  async ready({ page }) {
    return page.evaluate(() => Boolean(window.myFeature?.ready));
  },
  async run({ page, outDir }) {
    await page.getByText("Expected output").waitFor();
    return { assertion: "passed" };
  },
  async cleanup({ page, state }) {
    // Remove only fixtures created by run().
  },
};
```

`run()` starts only after the standard DG runtime proof and any caller readiness hook succeeds. `cleanup()` runs when `run()` started, including after a failed assertion. Return JSON-serializable proof values.

## Options

- `--slot 1|2|3`: Select the Roam account/profile.
- `--skip-build`: Load the existing `apps/roam/dist` without rebuilding.
- `--headed`: Run with a visible Chromium window.
- `--keep-open`: Leave the browser open after loading.
- `--dist <path>`: Load a different Roam extension folder. Use only when intentionally testing another build output.
- `--registration-name <name>`: Developer Extensions row name. Defaults to the built folder name, usually `dist`.
- `--test-module <path>`: Caller readiness, test, and cleanup hooks. Absolute Windows paths and paths containing spaces are supported.
- `--out <path>` and `--screenshot-name <name>`: Proof artifact locations.
- `--timeout <ms>`: UI and readiness timeout. Defaults to `45000`.

## Folder Loading

Roam Depot's folder button calls `window.showDirectoryPicker()`, not an `<input type="file">`. The script installs a temporary in-page directory-picker shim backed by the files in `apps/roam/dist`.

The loader uses native Playwright clicks for developer mode and folder controls. It treats the extension row as registration only, then clicks the header or row refresh control when present and waits for DG runtime proof. Roam versions that activate automatically may expose no refresh control.

An IndexedDB clone warning for the fake directory handle is expected and classified separately. Other page exceptions fail the run. `last-run.json` includes phase timings and bounded browser diagnostics; failures also capture a dedicated screenshot and compact DOM state.

## Safety Notes

- Do not commit `.env`, browser profiles, or artifacts.
- Do not commit real Roam test account emails, graph names, graph URLs, or proof screenshots.
- Keep feature fixtures, command interactions, and assertions in the caller module. Do not add them to the generic loader.

input.content:
---
name: reference_roam_loader_canvas_driving
description: Driving the Roam tldraw canvas from playwright:load-extension needs a dev build, the settings dialog closed, and the camera centred per shape
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Three things block `pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension --test-module` from driving the Roam tldraw canvas. All three fail *silently* as clean false negatives, not errors.

1. **`window.tldrawApps[pageTitle]` is the editor handle, but only in a dev build.** `apps/roam/scripts/build.ts` defaults `NODE_ENV` to `production`, which compiles the registration out entirely (`grep -c tldrawApps dist/extension.js` → 0). Build with `NODE_ENV=development npx tsx scripts/build.ts`, run the loader with `--skip-build`, then rebuild production afterwards so the worktree's `dist` is not left a dev artifact.
2. **The loader leaves the Roam settings dialog open** after its DG proof step. Every canvas click lands on the modal overlay instead. Press Escape until `.bp3-dialog, .bp3-overlay-open` is gone, in `ready()` *and* after the canvas mounts.
3. **Centre the camera per shape before clicking.** `zoomToFit()` across a row of fixtures puts the outer ones off-canvas or under the style panel; `editor.setCamera({x: -midX + 400, y: -midY + 300, z: 1})` makes every click land.

Always make the probe prove the menu opened before judging its contents — assert tldraw's own entries (`Duplicate|Delete|Copy as|Export as|Select all`) are present, else "menu did not open" scores as "menu without the item you're testing". A locked shape gets a reduced menu (no Duplicate/Delete), so include `Export as|Select all` in that marker.

Canvas pages are pages whose title matches `DEFAULT_CANVAS_PAGE_FORMAT` (`Canvas/*`), so a test module can make one with `roamAlphaAPI.data.page.create` and open it.

Related: [[reference_pr_evidence_worktree_roam_profile]], [[reference_pr_evidence_roam_login]], [[reference_tldraw_store_put_no_listener]], [[reference_roam_ext_dev_symlink_contested]]

content.text:
All four tasks done. Taking your two questions first, since the answers changed what I built.

## `getConvertibleShapeText` — fixed

The helper returned `null` / `""` / `"text"`, where **`""` meant "convertible" but is falsy**. Only images hit that branch. Any future caller writing the natural `if (shapeText)` would have silently dropped images from the Convert To menu and the `?C` dialog — no type error, the menu item just vanishes.

It's now two functions with no ambiguous value:

```ts
export const getShapeText = (shape: TLShape): string =>
  "text" in shape.props ? shape.props.text : "";

export const isConvertibleShape = (shape?: TLShape | null): boolean => { … }
```

The gate is a plain boolean, and the prefill is fetched only on the path that needs it — which also removed the oddity where the image path computed `shapeText` and threw it away.

**I did not touch `ImageConvertOverlay`.** Its `isConvertibleImage` is a TypeScript type guard (`shape is TLImageShape`) that the overlay depends on for narrowing; sharing would mean repeating the type check anyway. Still a drift risk, still your call.

## Live verification — 9 of 9, on a real graph

The credentials appeared in the main repo's `apps/roam/.env` since I last looked, so I pointed the worktree at them and at the signed-in `playwright-1` profile.

| Fixture | Convert To | |
|---|---|---|
| text shape (with text) | offered | regression check |
| text shape (empty) | offered | unchanged behavior |
| **rectangle with text** | **offered** | new |
| **sticky note with text** | **offered** | new |
| empty rectangle | absent | as designed |
| whitespace-only rectangle | absent | trim works |
| empty sticky note | absent | as designed |
| arrow with label | absent | still Relation only |
| locked rectangle | absent | |

**My first run reported a clean sweep of false negatives** — every fixture, including the pre-existing text case, came back "no Convert To". The loader leaves the Roam settings dialog open over the canvas, so every right-click hit a modal. I'd have reported a working feature as broken. The probe now asserts tldraw's own menu entries are present before judging, so "menu didn't open" can't be scored as "menu without Convert To"; that's what caught the locked case being inconclusive rather than passing.

I built with `NODE_ENV=development` to get the `window.tldrawApps` hook (production compiles it out), then **rebuilt production** so the worktree's `dist` isn't left a dev artifact. Nothing from the run is tracked — the proof modules live in gitignored `local/`.

## State

**CI: 9 passing, 0 failing, `MERGEABLE`/`CLEAN`.** The rebase needed no conflict resolution — GitHub's `CONFLICTING` was stale duplicate commits from a base force-push, including one the base had since reverted; `rebase --onto` dropped them. Both Codex threads fixed, replied to, resolved. PR body updated with the fixture table.

Two things still open: `reviewDecision` is `CHANGES_REQUESTED` from the original Codex pass and needs a re-review to clear, and **the automated run covers which shapes offer the option, not where the node lands**. The frame and group placement cases — the ones the delegated review caught me half-fixing — still want a hand-driven Loom before merge.

You are an expert senior software engineer specializing in modern web development, with deep expertise in TypeScript, React, Next.js (App Router), and Tailwind CSS. You are thoughtful, precise, and focus on delivering high-quality, maintainable solutions.

This repository uses Turborepo.

## Apps & Packages

`apps`

- apps/website: The public-facing website for Discourse Graphs, Uses Next.js.
- apps/roam: The Roam Research extension that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.
- apps/obsidian: The Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

`packages`

- packages/tailwind-config: Shared tailwind config
- packages/typescript-config: Shared tsconfig.jsons
- packages/eslint-config: ESLint preset
- packages/ui: Core React components

## Git & Publishing Conventions

### Agent-created Engineering tickets

For all agent-created Engineering tickets, including direct Linear tool calls and tickets created through other skills, use [dg-create-engineering-ticket](.agents/skills/dg-create-engineering-ticket/SKILL.md). Create them in `Ticket Draft` with exactly one workspace provenance label from the `Created by` group: `Created by Claude`, `Created by Codex`, or `Created by LLM` for another or unknown agent. Record the creation skills actually used in `Notes`, and verify those fields after creation. If no skill was used, record `Created with: direct agent workflow (no skill)` and still apply the same review rules.

The requesting human reviews intent, scope, acceptance criteria, and ticket-writing standards before approving a move to `Triage` or `Backlog`. Keep the provenance label after approval. See the skill for transitions and missing-configuration handling. This applies to new tickets; do not retrospectively classify existing tickets.

### Branch Naming

When working on Linear issues, prefer using the Linear-provided branch name when available. Linear automatically generates branch names in the format `eng-####-descriptive-name` (e.g., `eng-1912-scaffold-repocontent-model`).

- Use Linear's generated branch name for consistency and traceability
- Branch names should be lowercase with hyphens separating words
- Include the Linear ticket ID at the start of the branch name

### Pull Request Titles

PR titles for Linear-backed work should follow this format:

- Format: `ENG-#### Ticket title`
- The ticket ID must be uppercased (e.g., `ENG-1912` not `eng-1912`)
- Follow the ticket ID with the exact Linear ticket title
- Example: `ENG-1912 Scaffold @repo/content-model`

### Pull Request Bodies

When creating or updating a pull request body:

- Start with `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Preserve its headings and guidance instead of adding substitute sections.
- Treat the Linear ticket as the source of truth. Do not restate it in the pull request body.
- Do not add a file-by-file summary, implementation diary, investigation log, full command output, or unrelated pre-existing issues. For PRs over 400 changed lines, excluding tests, include a concise split justification, main review entry points, and testing path in Reviewer brief.
- Put line-specific implementation context in inline GitHub comments.
- Put any non-obvious rules that future changes must preserve in code comments, tests, or documentation, not only in the pull request.
- Remove empty optional sections and anything that does not help review the diff.

## Required standards

- Read and follow [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md) and the nested `AGENTS.md` files that apply to changed files before editing or reviewing code.
- Follow [PR_GUIDELINES.md](PR_GUIDELINES.md) for scope, verification, and review requirements. General code standards live in the style guide; app-specific instructions remain in nested `AGENTS.md` files.
- Before handoff or requesting review, run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` from `.agents/skills/dg-pr-adherence-check/SKILL.md` against the final diff and available PR metadata. Resolve findings or report them explicitly, including missing evidence. Rerun affected checks after changes.

content.text:
I can't record a Loom — that needs your account and their app — so I produced an mp4 instead: **41s, 10fps, captions burned in, visible cursor, paced for human reading.** It's above.

## What it shows

**Scene 1 — rectangle inside a frame.** Right-click → Convert To → Claim → Confirm. The green discourse node ends up inside the frame at the same spot.

| | parent | local x/y | page x/y |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | `shape:demo_frame` | 80,90 | 380,290 |
| after | `shape:demo_frame` | 80,90 | 380,290 |

Without `parentId`, tldraw would have read `80,90` as *page* coordinates and dropped the node near the canvas origin.

**Scene 2 — one of two grouped shapes.** The group dissolves exactly as `GroupShapeUtil.onChildrenChange` specifies, the node's parent becomes `page:page`, and the page point stays `320,240`. This is the case `parentId` alone did **not** cover: the child's group-relative x/y were `0,0`, so without the page-point fallback the node would have landed at page `0,0`. That's the half-fix the delegated review caught, now proven fixed.

## Two things the recording turned up

Both are real behavior worth knowing, and I've added them to the PR:

- **Clicking a grouped shape selects the group**, and Convert To is correctly not offered for a group — you have to enter the group first.
- **Double-clicking to enter a group also starts editing the shape's label**, so the first right-click after it just dismisses the editor rather than opening the menu. Cost me two runs before I stopped guessing and instrumented the selection state.

## State

PR body updated with the measured before/after numbers. Production `dist` restored (I'd built with `NODE_ENV=development` for the `window.tldrawApps` hook). The demo created two real Claim pages in the dev graph; cleanup deleted them along with the canvas pages.

The mp4 is at `local/roam-playwright/demo/` in the worktree — gitignored. `gh` can't attach video to a PR body, so **drag it into the PR comment box yourself** if you want it on #1431. The numeric evidence is already in the body either way.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about uploading video files to Loom programmatically:

## Loom Official Support

Video uploading is only available to users on Loom's Business, Business+ AI or Enterprise plans. However, the search results show that **Loom doesn't appear to offer a public API for programmatic video uploads**. The official Loom documentation only describes manual upload through their web interface where you click on New Video in the top right of your video library and select Upload Video.

## Video Format Requirements

If you do use Loom's upload feature, Loom supports containers like MV, AVI, WEBM, MP4, MOV (up to 4GB) and Loom limits uploads to 4 GB or 12 hours, whichever is less.

## Alternative Approaches

The search results show third-party solutions like Apify actors that can download videos from Loom, but these are for retrieving videos, not uploading them. If you need to programmatically create and upload video content similar to Loom, the search results also mention api.video as an alternative service that provides programmable video upload capabilities.

**Conclusion**: Based on available information, Loom does not appear to offer a public API for programmatic video file uploads. You would need to either use their web interface or explore alternative video hosting platforms that provide API upload functionality.

name: pr-evidence
description: Upload verification screenshots to the Roam dev graph and get public image URLs plus a Markdown table for the PR body. Use after a verification run produced PNGs and before create-pr writes the Evidence section.
---

# PR evidence upload

Uploads PNGs through `roamAlphaAPI.file.upload` in an authenticated Roam Playwright slot, files them under a page in the slot's graph (`discourse-dev-graph`), and emits a Markdown table that create-pr pastes into the Evidence section.

## When to use

- After verification (Roam `load-extension` run, Obsidian CDP run, manual captures) left PNGs on disk.
- Before create-pr builds the body. Roam PRs: reuse the verification's slot once that run has closed. Obsidian PRs: omit `--slot`.

## Command

Run from the worktree root, using the worktree's own `tsx` so the relative PNG paths and the repo's Playwright resolve:

```sh
./apps/roam/node_modules/.bin/tsx ~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/upload.ts \
  [--slot N] [--branch <b>] [--label "<YYYY-MM-DD · shortsha · harness>"] [--harness <name>] \
  [--out table.md] [--settle-ms 5000] \
  shot1.png="Empty state" shot2.png="After import" ...
```

- `pnpm --filter roam exec tsx ...` also works, but it changes cwd to `apps/roam`, so pass absolute PNG paths.
- `--branch` defaults to the current git branch. `--label` defaults to `<today> · <short sha> · <--harness or "manual">`.
- Caption defaults to the file name without extension.
- No `--slot`: tries each configured slot (1, 2, 3) and moves on only on a profile-lock error.
- Headless by default (`HEADLESS=false` to watch).

## Output contract

- stdout: JSON `{page, pageUid, branchBlockUid, runBlockUid, items: [{caption, url, blockUid}]}`.
- stderr: `Markdown table: <path>`. The file defaults to `pr-evidence-<runBlockUid>.md` next to the first PNG and contains `| Scenario | Screenshot |` rows with `![caption](url)`. create-pr pastes it as-is.
- URLs are public Firebase storage links (`200 image/png` without cookies, verified 2026-09-23).

## Roam structure

```
Trang test/                       (page, found or created)
  <branch>                        (top-level block, reused on every run)
    <date · sha · harness>        (new run block per invocation, appended last)
      <caption> ![](<url>)        (one per PNG)
```

## Gotchas

- Imports `apps/roam/scripts/playwright/roamSession.ts` from the current worktree (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), so profiles live in that worktree's `local/roam-playwright/profiles/` unless `DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_PROFILE_DIR_<n>` is set.
- A slot's profile can only be open once. Close the verification session first, never delete lock files.
- Login errors (expired session, 2FA) come from `openRoamSession`; recover with `pnpm --filter roam playwright:open -- --slot N --headed --allow-login`, then rerun.
- Never print values from `apps/roam/.env`.
- Uploads cannot be rolled back and Roam cannot list graph files, so don't loop retries on a failing run.
- tsx injects `__name()` into functions passed to `page.evaluate`; the script shims it in the page first. Keep that shim if you edit the in-page code.

content.text:
**No — there's no Loom MCP**, and it wouldn't help if there were. I checked both:

- The MCP registry returns nothing for loom/video/screen-recording (only PubMed and Figma, both irrelevant).
- **Loom has no public upload API.** Uploading is a manual web-UI action (`New Video → Upload Video`), and it's gated to Business/Business+/Enterprise plans. There are third-party Loom *downloader* APIs on Apify, but nothing for upload.

So no tool can put this in Loom for you. Three things that actually work, in order of how good the result is:

**1. Drag the mp4 into the PR comment box** — 349 KB, ~10 seconds of your time. GitHub uploads it to its own CDN and renders a real inline player with scrubbing. This is the only route to an embedded video on GitHub; the upload endpoint isn't in the public REST API, so `gh` can't do it.

**2. Let me embed it as a GIF, fully automated.** I already made one to check feasibility: **780 KB** at 900px wide, 8fps — small enough that `pr-evidence` can upload it to the dev graph and I can drop `![](url)` straight into the PR body, where GitHub renders it inline. No manual step. Trade-off: no scrubbing, no pause, and the captions are slightly softer at 900px. That's the realistic substitute for a Loom embed.

**3. Upload the mp4 itself via pr-evidence** — works and gives a public Firebase URL, but GitHub renders it as a plain link, not a player. Strictly worse than either of the above.

Worth saying plainly: the PR body already carries the *evidence* — measured parent ids and page coordinates before and after, for both the frame and the group case. The video is for reviewer confidence, not proof, so option 1 whenever you next have the PR open is probably the right call and costs me nothing.

Want me to do **2** now? It's the only one I can complete without you, and it's reversible — I'd just edit the image back out of the body if you'd rather drag the mp4 in later.

---
name: reference_pr_evidence_camo_broken
description: Roam file.upload now serves every file as application/octet-stream, so pr-evidence URLs fail GitHub's camo proxy and do not render in a PR
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Roam's `roamAlphaAPI.file.upload` serves **everything** as `content-type: application/octet-stream`, including PNGs. GitHub proxies external images through `camo.githubusercontent.com`, which requires an `image/*` content type and returns **400** otherwise, so `![](<firebase url>)` from `pr-evidence` renders as a broken image in a PR body.

Verified 2026-10-04 by POSTing the markdown to `gh api /markdown` and fetching the returned camo URL: 400 for both a `.png` and a `.gif` upload. The `pr-evidence` SKILL.md still claims "200 image/png without cookies, verified 2026-09-23", which is now stale.

Setting the type client-side does not help: `upload.ts` already passes `new File([...], name, { type: "image/png" })` and the served type is still octet-stream, so Roam or its storage layer overrides it. Patching `upload.ts` to infer the MIME from the extension is dead code — tried and reverted.

The links are still publicly reachable (HTTP 200), so they work as **download** links, just not as inline images.

For a video on a PR, there is no automated path: Loom has no public upload API (and upload is a paid-plan feature), no Loom MCP exists, and GitHub's own attachment upload is browser-only. Drag the file into the PR comment box by hand to get an inline player.

content.text:
Uploaded, but **it does not get you an inline video**, and the reason is worth knowing because it affects more than this PR.

## What happened

Both files are up and publicly reachable (HTTP 200):
- **mp4** (349 KB) — now linked in the PR body as a download
- **gif** (780 KB) — uploaded, but unusable for embedding, see below

## The blocker

Roam's `file.upload` serves **everything** as `content-type: application/octet-stream`. GitHub proxies external images through `camo.githubusercontent.com`, which requires `image/*` and returns **400** otherwise. I tested it rather than assuming: rendered the markdown via `gh api /markdown`, pulled the camo URL it generated, and fetched it.

```
GIF via camo → HTTP 400
PNG via camo → HTTP 400
```

**That second line is the important one.** It's not about video. A plain pr-evidence screenshot fails the same way, so **every `![](firebase…)` image in your recent PRs is almost certainly rendering broken on GitHub right now.** The skill's own contract still claims `200 image/png without cookies, verified 2026-09-23` — that's gone stale since.

I tried patching `upload.ts` to infer MIME from the extension. It made no difference: the file already went up as `image/png` and still came back octet-stream, so Roam or its storage layer overrides the client-side type. Dead code, so **I reverted it** — your skill file is byte-for-byte as it was.

## Where that leaves the video

There is no automated route to an inline video on this PR. Loom has no upload API, no Loom MCP exists, and GitHub's attachment upload is browser-only. The mp4 link in the body will download a 349 KB file a reviewer can play locally — that's the honest ceiling without you touching it. **Dragging the mp4 into the PR comment box is still the only way to get a real player**, and it stays ~10 seconds of work.

The PR's actual evidence — measured parent ids and page coordinates before and after, for both the frame and the group case — is unaffected and already in the body.

Recorded the camo finding to memory, since it'll silently bite the next PR that uses pr-evidence. Worth deciding separately whether that skill should switch to a host that sets real content types.

# Scope Check

Compare the completed change with its acceptance boundary. Return a copy-ready `Scope check` section unless the user requests the analysis too.

## Gather the Inputs

1. Resolve the Linear issue from an explicit `ENG-###` identifier, then from the PR or branch name. Fetch the issue with the Linear connector. If it is unavailable, ask for the ticket's `Problem`, `Solution`, and `Done When` sections.
2. Treat `Done When` as the acceptance boundary. Use `Problem` and `Solution` only to clarify that boundary, not to silently expand it.
3. Resolve the final change set from the supplied diff or PR. For a PR, inspect its metadata and complete diff. For the current branch, compare it with the PR base branch and include staged and unstaged changes.
4. Read linked decisions or ticket comments only when they explain an apparent scope expansion.

## Evaluate Scope

Map every material behavior or architectural change to a `Done When` criterion.

- Treat implementation details, tests, documentation, and generated files required to satisfy `Done When` as in scope.
- Flag broader abstractions, unrelated refactors, new dependencies, migrations, or support for cases not required by `Done When`.
- Do not treat a change as in scope only because it is useful or adjacent.

For each scope expansion, determine:

1. What broader abstraction or additional case was introduced?
2. Which current use case or ticket requires it, and why must it be included now rather than deferred?
3. Was anyone affected or consulted, and where is the discussion or decision recorded?

Do not invent missing justification. Mark it `Not documented` and recommend recording it in a Linear comment before the PR is merged.

## Format the Result

Use this form when the diff stays within scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: None.
```

Use this form when the diff expands scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: <what changed>
- Required now: <use case or ticket and why it cannot be deferred>
- Anyone affected or consulted: <Yes, No, or Not documented>
- Decision: <link to the discussion or decision, or `Not documented`>
```

If the ticket or diff cannot be resolved, leave the checkbox unchecked and state exactly what input is missing. Keep findings short and evidence-based.

Do not modify the issue, PR, or implementation unless the user explicitly asks.

# PR adherence check

Review the final change against the repository's current rules. Remain read-only unless the user authorizes fixes or PR updates. Do not post comments, request reviews, or change ticket status as part of this check.

## Resolve the evidence

1. Use the supplied PR or resolve the current branch's PR. Read its title, base and head commits, complete diff, body, checks, and review state. For local work, compare with the merge base of the intended PR base and include staged, unstaged, and relevant untracked files. Identify unavailable metadata and explicitly exclude unrelated local work.
2. Read root `AGENTS.md`, `STYLE_GUIDE.md`, `PR_GUIDELINES.md`, and `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Read nested `AGENTS.md` files applicable to every changed path. Resolve these from the target repository, not the skill's installation directory. If reviewing changes to the rules themselves, also inspect the base versions so removing a requirement cannot silently erase a finding.
3. Resolve the Linear ticket from an explicit identifier, then the PR or branch. Use the repository's `$scope-check` skill for the `Done When` boundary and its separate Scope check output. Missing ticket access or acceptance criteria blocks the scope conclusion, not independent standards checks.
4. Use command results and manual testing evidence tied to the reviewed revision. A checked box or successful unrelated CI job is not proof of all validation. Record the reviewed head and any local changes so stale evidence is identifiable.

## Evaluate adherence

- Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code to assess applicable TypeScript, UI, organization, comments, documentation, hygiene, and testing rules. Focus findings on introduced or modified code, not unrelated existing debt.
- Check title and branch conventions, ticket linkage, PR body requirements, size guidance, split justification, review entry points, testing evidence, Loom, and review/check status against `PR_GUIDELINES.md`.
- Distinguish mandatory rules from preferences. Words such as “prefer” and “ideally,” the 200-line target, and the five-file guideline need judgment. Above 400 changed lines, excluding tests, check for the required explanation and review guide rather than rejecting the size alone.
- Explain concerns briefly to the PR author so they can address them; formal rule citations and evidence for each finding are not required. Do not invent exceptions, team approval, testing outcomes, or video contents. If a required document is unavailable or rules conflict without a clear applicable resolution, report the gap instead of guessing.
- Respect workflow timing: missing Loom or review evidence can be reported as outstanding before requesting review while a draft is being prepared. Do not call future post-merge steps violations on an open PR.
- Keep scope expansions in Scope check. Verification is optional. Standards check only records whether the check ran.

## Return the result

Return a copy-ready section:

```markdown
## Standards check

- [x] Ran `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata.
```

The checkbox means the review ran, not that all requirements passed. If the diff cannot be resolved or the review could not run, leave it unchecked and tell the author what blocked it. Separately make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them; do not require these details in the PR body. Rerun affected checks after changes to code, rules, or PR metadata.

=== PR_GUIDELINES.md ===
# PR guidelines

This is the repository source for the DevOps PR process. Code standards live in [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md); agent instructions live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Production changes, releases, and work intake remain in DevOps.

## Scope and structure

- Use one PR per Linear ticket. You may batch very minor, unrelated changes of a few lines when they are low risk.
- Scope the ticket to one specific problem. If additional problems need attention, pause that additional work and check with the team or lead before implementing it.
- Use separate PRs for unrelated refactors, feature additions, dependency updates, and lint or style fixes. Keep scope to a single package or app when possible.
- For features spanning packages, make foundational changes such as types and shared utilities first, then use separate PRs for usage and integration.

## Size and review guidance

About 200 added plus removed lines is a useful target. Up to 400 lines is acceptable when the change is scoped and self-contained. Ideally, touch fewer than five files; repetitive mechanical changes can justify more. These are review guidelines, not automatic rejection thresholds.

Test changes do not count toward the 400-line threshold.

Above 400 changed lines, explain why the PR cannot reasonably be split. Include the main review entry points and intended testing path in Reviewer brief. Keep this concise rather than adding a file-by-file summary.

## Branches and PR metadata

- Use Linear's generated branch name through Copy Branch Name.
- For Linear-backed work, use `ENG-#### Exact Linear ticket title` as the PR title. This is the repository convention in place of the alternative title formats previously listed in DevOps.
- Start with [.github/pull_request_template.md](.github/pull_request_template.md). Treat the ticket as the source of truth rather than restating it. Follow the PR body guidance in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#pull-request-bodies).

## Before requesting review

- Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm ci:validate` from the repository root before opening a PR or declaring it ready. Resolve failures before requesting review. A draft must disclose unresolved validation blockers.
- Check applicable build and lint commands. Manually exercise changed behavior end-to-end, including relevant edge cases and alternative flows. Verification is optional; use it when checks and results help the reviewer.
- Read the complete final diff and review it against [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md), including added and modified comments. Use inline PR comments for review-specific explanations and durable code comments for constraints future changes must preserve.
- Run `$scope-check` against the ENG ticket and final diff. Paste its Scope check section into the PR body. If `Done When` is missing, leave the checkbox unchecked and state that explicitly.
- Run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata. Check the Standards check box when it has run. Make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them.
- Complete the Local delegated full review required by the template, using `$dg-delegated-full-review` when no other full-review workflow is available.
- Include a Loom video for every PR, including backend, refactor, and infrastructure changes. Keep it under 2–3 minutes, show before/after for bug fixes, and narrate key decisions. Put the link in Loom video.
- Assign a reviewer when ready. Do not mark a draft ready while required evidence or reviews remain incomplete.

## After merge

Delete the PR branch after a successful merge. Creating a draft does not authorize merging or deleting branches.

8:- Use explicit return types for functions
9:- Avoid `any` types when possible
10:- Prefer arrow functions over regular function declarations

34:Keep comments that explain non-obvious decisions, external API or data constraints, known limitations, side effects, or ordering requirements. Prefer descriptive names when they can convey the same information.
36:Before keeping a comment, check:
48:Put implementation history, review iterations, scope justifications, and ticket splits in inline GitHub comments. Keep durable constraints and known limitations in code or linked documentation. Link to the decision when describing behavior as agreed or accepted.
50:Agents must check added and modified comments against these criteria before handoff. Authors must review them manually before requesting review.

81:  // ❌ Needs a comment to explain
107:## Documentation
111:## Code hygiene
113:- Remove unused imports, temporary comments, and debug logging before requesting review. Preserve intentional operational logging.
116:## Testing

- Result: right-clicking a sticky note or a shape with text on the canvas offers Convert To, prefilled with that shape's text. Empty ones do not offer it. Text and image shapes behave as before.
- Review focus: `isConvertibleShape` in `apps/roam/src/components/canvas/convertShapeToDiscourseNode.ts` is now the single gate, replacing the `isTextSelected || isImageSelected` pair that lived in both the context menu and the `?C` dialog. The positioning block in `replaceShapeWithDiscourseNode` is the riskiest hunk: it decides whether the new node keeps its parent or falls back to a page point.
- Risk or follow-up: no unit tests, see Standards check. Arrows bound to a converted shape still unbind and dangle, which is pre-existing for text and image shapes but easier to hit now that sticky notes and rectangles convert.

Stacked on #1427, which extracted `replaceShapeWithDiscourseNode`. #1427 merges first.

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` then `pnpm ci:validate` from the repository root: 6 of 6 tasks, exit 0.

Convert To is offered for a text shape with and without text, a rectangle with text, and a sticky note with text. It is absent for an empty rectangle, a whitespace-only rectangle, an empty sticky note, an arrow with a label, and a locked rectangle. The probe asserts tldraw's own menu entries are present before judging, so a menu that fails to open cannot be scored as a menu without Convert To.
- Placement, converting through the dialog and reading the shape records before and after:
  - Inside a frame: parent unchanged, local x/y `80,90` unchanged, page x/y `380,290` unchanged. Without `parentId` the node would have been placed at page `80,90`.
  - Inside a two-shape group: the group dissolves, the node's parent becomes `page:page`, and the page point stays `320,240`. Without the page-point fallback the node would have landed at page `0,0`, because the child's group-relative x/y were `0,0`.
- Clicking a grouped shape selects the group, and Convert To is correctly not offered for a group. Entering the group by double-click also starts editing the shape's label, so the first right-click after it only dismisses the editor.

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-1884 and the final diff.

(2) is a pre-existing placement bug that this change makes materially easier to hit, since sticky notes and rectangles are far likelier than text shapes to sit inside a frame or group. Shipping the widened gate without it would place nodes in the wrong spot.
- Anyone affected or consulted: not documented.
- Decision: not documented. Worth a line on ENG-1884 before merge.

Outstanding: no unit tests. `isConvertibleShape` and `getShapeText` are pure functions and `STYLE_GUIDE.md` asks for unit tests on new functionality. `apps/roam/vitest.config.mts` only includes `src/utils/__tests__` and `scripts/__tests__`, so covering a file under `src/components/canvas` means either placing the test in `src/utils/__tests__` or widening that glob. Flagging the choice rather than making it here.

## Local delegated full review

- [x] Ran a comprehensive review of the entire final diff in a subagent with a fresh context, using `$dg-delegated-full-review`.

It found no high or medium regressions. Its one substantive finding, that passing `parentId` alone did not cover a dissolving two-shape group, is fixed in 13757e93 and verified above.

Identify unavailable metadata and explicitly exclude unrelated local work.
2. Read root `AGENTS.md`, `STYLE_GUIDE.md`, `PR_GUIDELINES.md`, and `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Read nested `AGENTS.md` files applicable to every changed path. Resolve these from the target repository, not the skill's installation directory. If reviewing changes to the rules themselves, also inspect the base versions so removing a requirement cannot silently erase a finding.
3. Resolve the Linear ticket from an explicit identifier, then the PR or branch. Use the repository's `$scope-check` skill for the `Done When` boundary and its separate Scope check output. Missing ticket access or acceptance criteria blocks the scope conclusion, not independent standards checks.
4. Use command results and manual testing evidence tied to the reviewed revision. A checked box or successful unrelated CI job is not proof of all validation. Record the reviewed head and any local changes so stale evidence is identifiable.

## Evaluate adherence

- Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code to assess applicable TypeScript, UI, organization, comments, documentation, hygiene, and testing rules. Focus findings on introduced or modified code, not unrelated existing debt.

- Explain concerns briefly to the PR author so they can address them; formal rule citations and evidence for each finding are not required. Do not invent exceptions, team approval, testing outcomes, or video contents. If a required document is unavailable or rules conflict without a clear applicable resolution, report the gap instead of guessing.

- Keep scope expansions in Scope check. Verification is optional. Standards check only records whether the check ran.
